verdict.left_looks: A sandstone-block (cobble-stone-brick style) two-storey frontage with a crenellated parapet-style top edge, a dome/rounded cap rising above the roofline on one side and a squared tower block on the other. The street face has a striped orange-and-white awning across the ground floor, with a row of wooden crate/barrel-like blocks, dark purple-maroon sacks or stalls, and a few shrubs at the corners. Rust-red and grey-striated horizontal bands separate the storeys. Windows are small and few; the ground floor has an open central doorway. Side views show a flat sandstone base plinth, the awning continuing along one flank, and the upper parapet with small rooftop details. Materials are cohesive and sandy, with clear layering and a lively market character.
verdict.right_looks: A large, low, flat-roofed sandstone-walled block with a terracotta-red (orange-brown) render panel filling most of each facade. Sandstone pilasters and a wide sandstone cornice/parapet frame the walls, with a row of dark grey merlon-like blocks along the top edge. The front has a symmetrical arrangement: two wide red wall panels with small window openings, a recessed central entrance with grey pillars, a red carpet, and lanterns. Side and back views repeat the same pattern: tall recessed window slots with grey pillar inserts, a plain base plinth with decorative rosette blocks. The massing is one big rectangular box with very little roof or silhouette variation; the colour contrast is strong but the surfaces read as flat, uniform panels.
verdict.why: The left build has a layered silhouette (dome, tower, parapet), a striped awning, and visible storey bands that give it market-street character, while the right build is a single flat box of uniform red panels with little roof or depth variation.
